newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of France cuts interest rate.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of France cuts interest rate.

text.p: The following are economists' comments on the Bank of France's announcement on Thursday it was cutting its intervention rate to 3.25 percent from 3.35 percent.
It was a bit of a surprise for the markets as a whole.
They (the Bank of France) did not follow the Bundesbank entirely (after the last German repo rate cut) and now they have cashed in on that.
It means the Bank of France did not see the budget as being a threat in terms of inflation or the franc.
SONJA GIBBS, BOND STRATEGIST, NOMURA INTERNATIONAL
It's not terribly unexpected but what it does do is suggest there's scope for rates to come down further.

By only catching up with the Bundesbank they've signalled they're being cautious. They could have done more and been OK, but M3 and Ifo were both negative and perhaps weakness in the dollar made them more cautious.

It is a validation of the budget. But the Bank of France seems to have nearly used up its room to ease if the Bundesbank does not lower its repo rate. At best, the Bank of France could ease by another five basis points.
That does not mean that rates are going to rise. Rates are going to remain at their low level at least during 1997.
